source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
Pest and disease management on corn aims to protect the crop from damage caused by biotic stress factors and to help the crop grow well and achieve high yield. Frequent exposure to biotic stress factors reduces yield, hurts farm profitability, and can affect household economy. Biotic stress factors include insect pests, diseases, weeds, water stress, and soil factors. Management and control methods vary by region.

Leaf Blight (ជំងឺទុំលឿងស្លឹក): Symptoms — leaves turn yellow, spreading from plant to plant via wind and rain; the disease develops fastest in cool weather. Control — use varieties resistant to this disease; cut and remove infected plant parts, burning and burying them away from the field; use protective fungicides such as Metalaxyl or other fungal disease treatments.

Pythium Stalk Rot (ជំងឺរលួយដើម): Symptoms — the plant is shorter than normal, with a water-soaked lesion at the middle of the stem or base, developing fastest in wet weather and causing wilting. Control — cut and remove infected plants by burning and burying away from the field; use protective fungicides such as Metalaxyl or other fungal treatments.

Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (ជំងឺរោគដំរៅដើម): Symptoms — begins from the leaf sheath upward, causing the affected area to become dry and wither, spreading rapidly under all conditions. Control — use resistant varieties; cut affected leaves or plant parts and burn/bury away from the field; use fungicides such as Benomyl, Carbendazim, Difenoconazole, and other fungal disease treatments.

Seed Rot (ជំងឺរលួយគ្រាប់ពោត): Caused by fungi and bacteria including Pythium, Fusarium, Diplodia, Rhizoctonia, and Penicillium spp. Symptoms — the embryo rots and dies before it can germinate and emerge. Control — store seed properly; sun-dry seed before planting; soak seed in warm water before planting; plow and dry the field thoroughly before planting.

Seedling Blight (ជំងឺស្លាកស្លឹកលើកូនពោត): Occurs on young seedlings shortly after emergence. Symptoms — seedlings show yellowish wilting, spotted leaves, and sudden death; affected seed shows white or pink coloring with fungal growth around it that causes the seed to rot. Contaminated seed or soil containing fungal pathogens causes this disease in seedlings. It commonly occurs when planting is delayed past the optimal window, and most often occurs in April and May. Well-drained soil, or soil that is not overly compacted, can reduce this disease. Control — treat seed before planting; improve field drainage systems; remove and burn infected plants.
